body.statement: Can the handle \(H_{\mathrm{transfer}}\) be completed, without using a formula for \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), so that for \(q<q_0\) and \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}<c b_n\) there exists one \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private estimator satisfying \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_P|T_{\mathrm{DP}}-\tau_P(x_0)|\le C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\)?
body.justification: This is the only remaining step from the matched privacy-leading theorem to a global incremental-price decomposition with a symbolic nonprivate benchmark.
body.gap: Kennedy's oracle inequalities do not imply neighboring-dataset stability, and Niu et al.'s sample-splitting guarantee does not transfer arbitrary nonprivate minimax risk.
body.consumer: A positive answer makes any future exact-uniform nonprivate improvement automatically compatible with the sharp privacy price; a negative answer identifies the necessary stability information beyond minimax risk.
